title: Introduce API Negotiator proxy and deprecation adapter for graceful schema transitions
author: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: We need a low-risk migration path for a planned contract change to the streaming and tool-call payload shapes (v2 -> v3) while preserving functionality for older clients. Previous approaches relied on ad-hoc backwards shims in model handlers which scattered logic and made rollbacks risky. This PR introduces a dedicated 'API Negotiator' proxy layer plus a deprecation adapter that centralizes schema translation, opt-in beta headers, and observability so we can run v3 by default while serving older clients for a period without runtime churn.

Scope and goals: central proxy that negotiates request/response schema versions, a translation adapter for legacy function/tool-calling payloads, streaming compatibility fallbacks, and a small set of metrics/logs/alerts to monitor regression. This is intentionally conservative: no model runtime changes, no customer-facing CLI changes.

What changed (high level):
- New proxy: src/proxy/negotiator.go - inspects X-Redwood-Schema-Version and X-Redwood-Schema-Beta headers, routes to v3 handlers when present, otherwise rewrites requests in-flight.
- Deprecation adapter: src/proxy/adapter/legacy_to_v3.go - transforms legacy 'functions' array to structured tool-calls, preserves tool metadata and converts streaming chunks to the v3 frame protocol when needed.
- Streaming polyfill: src/proxy/adapter/stream_polyfill.go - reassembles chunked v2 events for v3 consumer and emits synthetic end-of-stream where upstream lacks sentinel.
- Observability: added metrics (schema_negotiator.requests_total, negotiator.fallbacks_total, negotiator.latency_p90) and a debug log path for rewrites.
- Tests: unit tests and a small end-to-end harness that replays real production traces for v2 clients.
- Docs: docs/openai-compat/schema-migration.md with opt-in steps and example headers.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (negotiator.enabled = false).
2) Enable negotiator in staging and run trace replay e2e; watch negotiator.fallbacks_total and latency metrics.
3) Soft launch: enable negotiator.enabled = true and require X-Redwood-Schema-Beta for a subset of internal customers.
4) Gradual ramp (2 weeks) after validation; monitor for structured-output regressions and tool-call failures.
5) Deprecation notice to customers and a 60-day tail for legacy translation before sunsetting.

Testing and validation: added unit coverage for adapter transformations, integration tests for streaming boundary cases (chunk reordering, missing sentinels), and a trace-replay smoke test using 200 sampled production requests. CI initially failed due to a flaky e2e harness; I fixed ordering in the harness and re-ran.

Backward compatibility notes: legacy clients that do not opt-in keep a functionally identical experience via translation. The adapter emits "X-Redwood-Warn: schema-deprecated" header on responses so clients can be notified. No model-serving container images were changed.

Migration guidance (docs summary): to opt in, include header X-Redwood-Schema-Beta: v3 and use new streaming frames as documented. See docs/openai-compat/schema-migration.md for examples and automated compatibility checks.

Related work and references: ENG-4281 (schema migration project), PM-712 (product roll plan), SUP-459 (support ticket for streaming regression discovered 2026-01-29).

release_notes: Add API Negotiator proxy and a legacy->v3 deprecation adapter to enable gradual schema rollout for streaming and tool-calling; opt-in via X-Redwood-Schema-Beta header; adds observability metrics and a migration guide.
